remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive. Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Portrait of Watson." Watson was a mechanic and friend of O'Keeffe, when she lived in Canyon, Texas, fall 1916 to late February 1918, as pointed out by Sarah Greenough in *Art and Letters* (1987), n. 69, p. 285. The orientation is a subject of debate. The work has been exhibited and/or reproduced as a vertical with the red area on the bottom right, and as a horizontal with the red area on the left. Orientation based on Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks.
titles.title: Portrait – W – No. I

description: A narrow, twisting black form encircles a small brushstroke of red before stretching horizontally across the canvas. Below this is another narrow black line, also wrapping around a small red brushstroke. Above and below these features is a soft, neutral background in shades of tan and blue. The entire composition appears soft and blurry, as though painted with a great deal of water mixed into the pigments.
title: Portrait – W – No. I
